plan.title: fix(authz): operator mint unreachable on Windows — CONIN$ probe opened read-only (#3110)

narratives.Description: On Windows, operator mint fails at the controlling-terminal probe because CONIN$ is opened read-only. Open CONIN$ with r+ on win32 for the probe and the phrase read, add a Windows regression test, and put --confirm on the three stale remediation strings. Do not weaken #3110.
narratives.Overview:
## Symptom

Operator mint appears **impossible on Windows**. In a real interactive PowerShell console, in
the repo worktree, with `--confirm` and no agent env markers:

```
PS C:\Repos\deft\directive\.deft-scratch\worktrees\issue-3438-shell-dest-form> task scope:record-approved-scope -- xbrief/active/<...>.xbrief.json --actor msadams --confirm
scope:record-approved-scope: refusing operator-cli stamp without a controlling terminal.
Open a real interactive console (not a headless/agent pipe) to mint (#3110).
```

The gate checks in order (`packages/cli/src/human-presence-mint.ts`): agent env markers → TTY
→ `--confirm` → **controlling terminal** → typed phrase. Reaching this message means the env
and TTY checks *passed* — so the console is real and the failure is specifically the
controlling-terminal probe.

## Probable cause

`defaultHasControllingTerminal()` does:

```ts
const path = process.platform === "win32" ? "CONIN$" : "/dev/tty";
const fd = openSync(path, "r");
```

On Windows, the console input device generally must be opened with **read/write** access;
`openSync("CONIN$", "r")` (O_RDONLY) commonly fails regardless of how the console was
launched. If that is what is happening, the probe fails in *every* Windows console and mint is
unreachable on the platform.

`defaultReadInteractiveConfirm()` opens the same device with the same `"r"` flag, so the phrase
read would likely fail too even if the probe were bypassed.

## Diagnostic

One line in a real Windows console distinguishes "wrong flag" from "wrong terminal":

```powershell
node -e "const{openSync,closeSync}=require('fs');for(const f of ['r','r+']){try{closeSync(openSync('CONIN$',f));console.log(f,'OK')}catch(e){console.log(f,'FAIL',e.code)}}"
```

- `r FAIL` + `r+ OK` → confirms the flag is the bug; fix is `"r+"` on win32 for both the probe
  and the read.
- both FAIL → the console genuinely is not attached (different root cause; investigate whether
  go-task replaces the console handles before the engine spawns, even though
  `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` uses `stdio: "inherit"`).
- both OK → the failure is elsewhere and this issue needs re-scoping.

## Impact

Blocking, and platform-wide if confirmed. `verify:scope-provenance` requires an approved-scope
digest, minting requires a human TTY by design (#3110, correctly), and if the Windows probe
cannot succeed then **no Windows operator can ever satisfy the gate** — `task check` cannot
pass on any change that touches an active xBRIEF's file scope. Encountered while trying to land
#3588.

## Secondary defect (same area, independent)

Three remediation strings tell the operator to run a command that always fails, because they
omit `--confirm`:

- `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` ~line 281 (`remediationForExpansion`)
- same file, ~lines 437 and 457
- `tasks/scope.yml` lines 164-165 (usage comments)

`packages/cli/src/scope-record-approved-scope.ts:66` (usage) and
`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/intent-evaluate.ts:75` (remint) do include it, so the fix
is to make the three stale strings consistent.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Diagnostic run in a real Windows console and its result recorded here
- [ ] If flag-related: `"r+"` on win32 for both `defaultHasControllingTerminal` and
      `defaultReadInteractiveConfirm`, with a Windows regression test
- [ ] Mint demonstrated end-to-end on Windows (a real operator mints a digest)
- [ ] The three remediation strings include `--confirm`
- [ ] No weakening of #3110: env-marker, TTY, `--confirm`, and typed-phrase requirements all
      stay exactly as they are — this is a platform-probe fix, not a policy change

Refs #3110, #3145, #3205, #3588.
